stages.name: Requirements
stages.entryQuestion: Before designing a home news feed, what scope and scale assumptions would you clarify?
stages.objective: Agree on product behavior, measurable quality targets and the stated exercise workload.

completionCriteria.name: Functional scope
completionCriteria.guidance: Define following, eligibility, deletion and ordering; a chronological feed is valid, and media bytes are outside this problem.

completionCriteria.name: Quality targets
completionCriteria.guidance: Clarify freshness, pagination stability and privacy guarantees separately from read availability.

completionCriteria.name: Capacity estimates
completionCriteria.guidance: Use the fictional baseline or state a justified alternative; derive average and peak rates and distinguish payload bytes from replication and indexes.

stages.name: High Level Design
stages.entryQuestion: Walk me through publishing a post and reading a follower home feed.
stages.objective: Separate post truth, relationship truth, fanout work and read assembly.

completionCriteria.name: Publication truth
completionCriteria.guidance: Durably store posts and a replayable publication event before acknowledging.

completionCriteria.name: Graph ownership
completionCriteria.guidance: Maintain follow, block and privacy state with clear authorization checks.

completionCriteria.name: Read assembly
completionCriteria.guidance: Assemble eligible candidates from bounded feed references and author streams, then hydrate post metadata.

stages.name: Core Flow
stages.entryQuestion: How would you combine ordinary-author fanout with million-follower authors and stable pagination?
stages.objective: Design a high-degree-aware feed assembly flow with defensible cursor semantics.

completionCriteria.name: Hybrid candidate strategy
concepts: Push ordinary authors or justified alternative
completionCriteria.guidance: Choose write/read/hybrid fanout with a clear high-degree author policy; estimate its amplification rather than requiring one fixed threshold.

completionCriteria.name: Fanout replay
completionCriteria.guidance: Use stable post/event IDs and idempotent reference insertion, with a cutoff rule for follow/unfollow races.

completionCriteria.name: Ordering and pagination
completionCriteria.guidance: Use a stable tie-breaker and cursor watermark/snapshot or a justified alternative that bounds duplicates and skipped items while new posts arrive.

completionCriteria.name: Candidate filtering
completionCriteria.guidance: Apply current blocks, deletions and private-account eligibility before returning hydrated results.

stages.name: Data Model
stages.entryQuestion: What data models and indexes support author timelines, follows and home-feed cursors?
stages.objective: Model authoritative social state separately from derived feed materializations.

completionCriteria.name: Post and author stream
completionCriteria.guidance: Store post ID, author, ordering key, visibility version and deletion marker; index the author timeline.

completionCriteria.name: Social relationships
completionCriteria.guidance: Support follower enumeration for fanout and following enumeration for reads, with versioned follow/block changes.

completionCriteria.name: Feed materialization
completionCriteria.guidance: Store bounded recipient-post references rather than copying whole post bodies; identify the rebuild source.

stages.name: Reliability
stages.entryQuestion: What happens when fanout falls behind or a user blocks an author whose posts are cached?
stages.objective: Protect eligibility while recovering derived feed state.

completionCriteria.name: Durable recovery
completionCriteria.guidance: Replay publication work and rebuild derived feeds from post and relationship truth after worker/cache failure.

completionCriteria.name: Privacy correctness
completionCriteria.guidance: A stale cache cannot grant access; validate visibility or use versioned invalidation with a defined bound.

completionCriteria.name: Degraded reads
completionCriteria.guidance: Define bounded stale-but-eligible reads, backpressure and fallback when rankers or high-degree streams fail.

stages.name: Scaling
stages.entryQuestion: How would you size reads and fanout for normal authors while isolating a celebrity post?
stages.objective: Budget write amplification and read hydration, not just incoming post requests.

completionCriteria.name: Rate amplification
completionCriteria.guidance: Derive 23.15 average posts/s and 2314.81 average page reads/s; 100 ordinary followers imply 200 million reference writes/day before high-degree exceptions.

completionCriteria.name: Hot-author isolation
completionCriteria.guidance: Shard fanout work by recipient range and bypass or batch high-degree authors; avoid one queue partition owning all celebrity work.

completionCriteria.name: State budget
completionCriteria.guidance: A 500-reference feed for 20 million active recipients contains 10 billion references, about 160 GB at 16 bytes each before overhead and replicas.

stages.name: Tradeoffs
stages.entryQuestion: Which tradeoffs would you choose for freshness, ranking and consistency?
stages.objective: Explain how the chosen design changes product behavior under load.

completionCriteria.name: Read/write tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Compare fanout cost, read aggregation and freshness for normal versus high-degree authors.

completionCriteria.name: Ranking tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: A chronological baseline is acceptable; if ranking is used, define stable cursor/version semantics and a latency fallback.

completionCriteria.name: Eligibility tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Explain consistency for privacy versus eventual feed insertion and choose useful freshness, queue-lag and filtering metrics.
